chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mu'azi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalesi, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever performs Hajj ten times, God will not call him to account ever.

key_terms.لَمْ يُحَاسِبْهُ: He will not call him to account / reckon with him

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing Hajj ten times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith emphasizes the cumulative spiritual merit of performing Hajj ten times, promising exemption from divine reckoning (*hisab*) on the Day of Judgment. In Shia tradition, this 'exemption' is often understood as a complete pardon from minor sins or a simplified accounting, reflecting the transformative power of sustained devotion and the intercessory role of the Imams in facilitating such rewards.
